opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll is within the allowed maximum (write for full-time employees), so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record shows Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; write is above the allowed maximum, so I recommend granting read.
reason: HR (authoritative for employment status) verified Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Per policy, full-time employees max out at write, and admin would require the role to own the system (Engineer owns Source Code, not Payroll), so the maximum for Payroll is write. The requested write access is at the maximum and not above it, so I grant write. (Note: Security's record lists contractor status, but HR's verified employment record is authoritative; even so, granting the requested level write is within the max under the HR-confirmed full-time status.)
